name: Web document — News article
description: A recognizable news article on a transparent overlay, as a clean backdrop for the channel's hand-pulled highlight. Faithful site look BY DESIGN: a publication-neutral light editorial page (white #ffffff) with a colored uppercase publication/section kicker, a large serif headline, a 'By Author · date' byline, a rule, and serif body paragraphs, inside a browser window whose address bar shows the URL — NO Syntax collage chrome (no torn edge / grit / hard offset shadow), and NO CSS glow on the captured card. Because the page is light, the highlight runs in the light (multiply) blend mode — the dark body type stays readable under the amber band, like on paper. The emissive 'web page on a backlit display' look is a TypeGPU shaderPass (subpixel emission, backlight bloom, escaping-bezel halo, viewport-edge defocus), not Pack chrome. ~6s: card settles in, the highlighter draws over the hero line (~1.2→2.4s), then a long static hold a creator can freeze/extend. Transparent WebM overlay, composited over footage.

content.title: The real reason your build got slow — and the one-line fix
content.author: Jordan Lee
content.body: For months, teams across the industry blamed their bundlers for ballooning build times. A closer look at one widely-shared case suggests a humbler culprit. [highlight]The entire slowdown traced back to a single console.log running inside a hot loop[/highlight], firing once for every file in the project. Removing the line cut the build from forty seconds to nine.
